note: The BCB states (LBA 49184, 4 sectors) from which p10-enter may write the BCB command. Add a state only from a fresh read-only dump (p10-enter dump) of the unit, with an Opus review and the owner's approval. Never add a state that was not read from a unit. Unit 2's normal BCB (sha256 529bdb7b...) is here from the read-only dump of 2026-10-30 (M-1); it needs the Opus diff review of its commit and the owner's approval before use. The archive states afaa05c4... and fecfe0e2... are NOT here: their cause is unknown and they may be from unit 1.

states.name: zero
states.source: 2048 zero bytes. The state of the first misc backup (misc-bcb4-orig in the archive, hashed by the owner 2026-10-29); accepted by ucp10/tools/p10-bcb-fastboot.sh.

states.name: bootonce-bootloader
states.source: The payload: "bootonce-bootloader" and 2029 zero bytes, as built by ucp10/tools/p10-bcb-fastboot.sh. The same sha256 as the archive dumps misc-bcb4-bootloader/-bootonce/-check/-clean/-verify (hashed by the owner 2026-10-29). Seen when the command was written and not yet used by U-Boot; the tool then does not write again.

states.name: unit2-normal
states.source: Unit 2's normal BCB, read by p10-enter dump (read only) from mainline A on 2026-10-30 (M-1, P10-ENTER-M1.md); the same bytes as sectors 32-35 of a by-hand read of misc. The first sector is all zero, so the command field is empty: no command is pending. Sectors 2-4 hold data that is not a command (the review's F17: left in the BCB by U-Boot). The rockusb route writes the payload over it (the data in sectors 2-4 becomes zero) and does not restore it; bcb-before.bin in the log folder keeps it.
